concept.name: Clustering
concept.definition: Unsupervised partitioning or grouping of observations so members of the same cluster are more similar under a chosen representation and distance or linkage rule.
concept.intuition: It is a learnable mapping or representation used to turn features into predictions or groups.
concept.mechanics: Choose features, scaling, similarity, and algorithm; fit clusters without target labels; then assess stability and economic interpretation out of sample.
concept.failure_modes: Flexible models can fit noise, shift under new regimes, and conceal instability when tuning is repeated on the same validation data.
concept.misconceptions: Greater model complexity or in-sample accuracy does not by itself imply better out-of-sample trading results.
concept.example: Assets represented by return correlations are grouped into four clusters without supplying sector labels.
